## Root hunter timing and limitations

The retained `timing/plan.json` declared exactly three runs after all root-owned tests/economies exited: one original uninstrumented current trial, then one baseline and one current thread-CPU diagnostic. No favorable repeat, browser or other root-owned heavy task ran during measurement. Every sample and half-second host snapshot is retained.

| Original uninstrumented case | Warm p95 ms | Maximum ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Idle | 0.038339 | 0.174528 |
| Investigate | 1.064735 | 2.198930 |
| Pursue | 0.702077 | 0.909063 |
| Earned043 overlap | 0.610825 | 1.109514 |
| Nearby two | 0.962803 | 1.720085 |
| Fleet screen | 1.165593 | 1.660958 |

All six warm-p95 values satisfy the unchanged **≤2 ms** criterion in this exact-source trial; it is a percentile criterion, not a maximum criterion. Host load was 2.55→2.51. The author's separate high-load failed trial remains valid evidence, including investigate 9.883/pursue 4.049/nearby-two 2.620/fleet-screen 5.654 ms p95 under load 15.88→15.57. Root's pass does not prove the cause of those failures or certify all machines/frame pacing. Operation-count reduction and this trial's wall-time pass are separate conclusions. No further hunter optimization is assigned merely to replace the earlier unfavorable result.

The two additional instrumented diagnostics have strongly quantized per-call `process.threadCpuUsage` increments, including many zero/~4 ms values. Those per-call percentiles are **not valid fine-grained CPU attribution** and must not be subtracted from wall percentiles. Their wall timings are diagnostic, not a controlled hardware speedup or the acceptance population. All samples are retained; no additional timing run was made to repair this measurement limitation.
